initiatives.name: 2025 Organisational Restructuring and Facility Consolidation
initiatives.summary: Spirax Group implemented organisational changes and manufacturing facility consolidation in 2025, including EMEA simplification and site closures, delivering annualised savings of £40 million with approximately half realised in 2025. Implementation costs of £40 million were taken as a restructuring charge, with savings mostly reinvested into growth priorities.

evidence.title: Material Restructuring Programme in 2025
evidence.summary: The Group undertook significant restructuring in 2025, resulting in £37.0 million of restructuring costs classified as adjusting items, up from nil in 2024. The Audit Committee specifically scrutinised and approved the Adjusting items policy and its application given the scale of this restructuring.
evidence.quote: Given the significant restructuring in 2025, the Committee focused on scrutinising and approving the Adjusting items policy and its application.

evidence.title: STS EMEA Organisational Simplification
evidence.summary: STS simplified its organisational structure in EMEA, reducing from 19 individually managed operating companies to 10, while continuing to serve 23 countries. This reduced management layers and consolidated technical sales and service capabilities, contributing to accelerated organic sales growth in the region.
evidence.quote: In STS, we successfully implemented a simplification of our organisational structure in the EMEA region, moving from 19 individually managed operating companies to 10, continuing to serve 23 countries and maintaining our local, direct sales capability while reducing management layers.

evidence.title: Manufacturing Footprint Optimization - Site Closures and Relocations
evidence.summary: Following a review of manufacturing footprint and product portfolio, Spirax Group closed its STS facility in Mexico (production transferred to USA), paused Gestra facility expansion in Germany, and closed the Alitea pump facility in Sweden (production moved to UK). The company also began transferring UK-manufactured components to the USA to support 'Build America, Buy America' Act compliance.
evidence.quote: Following a review of our manufacturing footprint and product portfolio, focused on optimising what we make and where we make it, we completed the closure of our STS facility in Mexico with production transferred to the USA...In parallel, we closed our higher-cost Alitea pump facility in Sweden, transferring production to the UK.

evidence.title: 2025 Organisational Restructuring Delivering £40m Annualised Savings
evidence.summary: Spirax Group implemented organisational changes and manufacturing facility consolidation in 2025, including EMEA simplification and site closures, delivering annualised savings of £40 million with approximately half realised in 2025. Implementation costs of £40 million were taken as a restructuring charge, with savings mostly reinvested into growth priorities.
evidence.quote: The organisational changes and consolidation of manufacturing facilities implemented in 2025 will deliver annualised savings of £40 million, with approximately half realised in 2025. Implementation costs of £40 million have been taken as a restructuring charge in 2025, of which £33 million were cash costs and £7 million were non-cash charges.

initiatives.name: Decarbonisation Growth Initiatives: TargetZero and PoweringZero
initiatives.summary: Spirax Group is pursuing significant market expansion through decarbonisation solutions - TargetZero (steam generation electrification, adding ~£2bn addressable market) and PoweringZero (broader thermal energy decarbonisation, adding ~£5bn addressable market), via new technologies like SteamVolt, Electrofit, Steam Battery and High-Temperature Heat Pumps.

timeline.latest_update: FY2025 Annual Report; strategy set at Capital Markets Day October 2024

evidence.title: Commercial Partnership for High-Temperature Heat Pump Technology
evidence.summary: Spirax Group entered a commercial partnership with a leading global provider of heat pumps to commercialize High-Temperature Heat Pump technology for steam generation using waste process heat, with six units currently being validated on customer sites.
evidence.quote: We have also made progress in the commercialisation of High Temperature Heat Pump technology for the generation of steam utilising waste process heat. Through a commercial partnership with a leading global provider of heat pumps, we have six units currently being validated on customer sites.

evidence.title: SteamVolt Technology Agreements with Global Boiler OEMs
evidence.summary: Spirax Group reached agreements with several global industrial Boiler OEMs to incorporate its SteamVolt technology into their electric boilers, with pilot solutions installed in Food & Beverage and Chemical plant facilities.
evidence.quote: We have reached agreement with several global industrial Boiler OEMs to incorporate our SteamVolt technology into their electric boilers, with our first pilot solutions installed in a Food & Beverage facility and a second one installed in a Chemical plant.

evidence.title: Decarbonisation Growth Drivers: TargetZero and PoweringZero
evidence.summary: Spirax Group is pursuing significant market expansion through decarbonisation solutions - TargetZero (steam generation electrification, adding ~£2bn addressable market) and PoweringZero (broader thermal energy decarbonisation, adding ~£5bn addressable market), via new technologies like SteamVolt, Electrofit, Steam Battery and High-Temperature Heat Pumps.
evidence.quote: Solutions we refer to as TargetZero add ~£2 billion to our annual addressable market...Solutions we refer to as PoweringZero add ~£5 billion to our annual addressable market as we continue to deploy our Low Voltage and Medium Voltage solutions in target sectors and regions to support the electrification of critical industrial processes that currently rely on the direct burning of fossil fuels today.

initiatives.name: One Planet Sustainability Roadmap
initiatives.summary: Following completion of the first five-year phase of the One Planet Sustainability Strategy (launched 2021), Spirax Group conducted a comprehensive refresh process including double materiality assessment, stakeholder engagement, and secured Board approval for the next phase roadmap in 2025.

evidence.title: One Planet Roadmap Sustainability Strategy Evolution
evidence.summary: The Group's sustainability strategy, previously termed 'One Planet: Engineering with Purpose', is evolving into the 'One Planet Roadmap', discussed regularly at Board level alongside completion of a materiality assessment confirming material sustainability topics are addressed through this program.
evidence.quote: One Planet: Engineering with Purpose Sustainability Strategy (moving forward as the One Planet Roadmap)... In 2025, the Group completed a materiality assessment and confirmed that material sustainability topics for the Group are addressed through One Planet.

evidence.title: One Planet Sustainability Roadmap Refresh and Board Approval
evidence.summary: Following completion of the first five-year phase of the One Planet Sustainability Strategy (launched 2021), Spirax Group conducted a comprehensive refresh process including double materiality assessment, stakeholder engagement, and secured Board approval for the next phase roadmap in 2025.
evidence.quote: 2025 marked the completion of the first phase of our One Planet Sustainability Strategy...The Board approved the refreshed One Planet Sustainability Roadmap...Major decisions in 2025 ranged from the approval of the Group's restructuring and revision to the One Planet Sustainability Roadmap to that of the interim and final dividend payments.

evidence.title: Net Zero Scopes 1&2 Emissions Target Achieved Early
evidence.summary: Spirax Group exceeded its 2025 interim target of 50% reduction in scopes 1 and 2 CO2e emissions (vs 2019 baseline), achieving 62% reduction (excluding acquisitions), and achieving the target a year early, as part of its journey to net zero by 2030.
evidence.quote: We achieved our One Planet net zero interim target to reduce our scopes 1 and 2 emissions (on a market basis) a year early and have continued to make further progress against our 2030 target. Excluding 2022 acquisitions, at 17,487 tonnes CO2e (tonnes) our emissions were 19% lower than 2024 and 62% lower than 2019.
